September    9    36.

Dear Mr. Barton,

In reply to your letter dated
September 3, 1936, I forward herewith
for your information a copy of a report
regarding Anson Chow alias Tseu Tao Feng.

Yours sincerely,

James Barton, Esq.,
H.B.M. Consulate-General,
Shanghai.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT
Date September 9, 1936.

Subject. Anson Chow alias Tseu Tao Feng.

Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

Anson Chow (鄒韜奮), generally known as Tseu Tao
Feng (韜奮), the principal shareholder in the Life
Publishing Company (生活書店 ), Lane 384, No.4 Foochow
Road, is at present editing and publishing a weekly magazine
entitled "The Livelihood" Weekly (生活星期刊 ) with an office
at Room 320, Shanghai Times Building, 160 Avenue Edward VII.
The first issue of this magazine appeared on June 7, 1936 in
Hongkong, which city Chow visited in May, 1936. His original
object in proceeding to Hongkong was to commence the publication
there of a daily paper entitled "Livelihood Daily Paper" but
failing to secure the necessary capital despite his appeal to
the public through the press, he decided to publish the "Liveli-
hood" Weekly. Finding that means of circulation in Hongkong
were not convenient, he moved to Shanghai and established an
editorial office at the present address in August publishing the
12th Issue of the "Livelihood" Weekly in Shanghai on August 23, 1936.
An application for registration of this magazine was
submitted on August 9, 1936, to the Ministry of the Interior
and the Propaganda Department of the C.E.C. of the Kuomintang,
but no certificate has been issued and it is learned that the
Chinese Authorities have expressed their intention to withhold
the certificate for the time being pending an examination of
the contents of several issues of this magazine.
Up to the present, only articles of a moderately anti-
Japanese nature have appeared in this magazine, which is sold
at five cents per copy. Some 20,000 copies of each issue are
printed.
Chow, aged about 38 and native of Changchow, is at present
staying at Lane 601, No.4 Rue Lafayette. He is a graduate of

Nanyang College, now known as the Kiaotung University. Between
1925 and 1930, he went to U.S.A. where he was engaged in
writing articles for periodicals. In 1931, after his return
to China, he came to public notice by writing anti-Japanese
articles in the "Life" Weekly ( 生活 ) following the
September 18 Incident.

    In January, 1933, he was elected a member of the
Executive Committee of the Shanghai Branch of the People's
Rights Protection League of China, which was inaugurated on
January 17, 1933 in the Central Reserach Institute, 331 Avenue
Roi Albert. This Branch embodied Leftist members of the
Kuomintang as well as followers of the Nationalist Party, and
its object was to safeguard the rights of free organization,
speech, press and assembly, and oppose the arrest of political
offenders of the Government. Chow did not take any active
part in the movement of the League which was subsequently
dissolved.

    A number of anti-Chiang Kai-shek articles appeared
in the "Life" Weekly towards the end of 1933 with the result
that it was banned by the National Government in December,
1933. Chow then left for Europe.

    In November, 1935, he returned to Shanghai and
published a new weekly known as the "People's Livelihood"
( 大众生活 ). This publication was suppressed by the
Chinese Authorities in February, 1936. Then he endeavoured
to promote a daily paper to be known as "Livelihood Daily
Paper" but this scheme did not meet with success, so he
turned his attention to thepublication of the "Livelihood"
Weekly now in circulation.
